newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs skyrocket on weak output data in late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGBs skyrocket on weak output data in late Tokyo.

text.p: Cash and futures Japanese government bonds (JGBs) skyrocketed in late trade on Friday after weak output forecasts for June and July, traders said.

The JGBs dipped briefly on an initial reaction to the May output data that showed a preliminary 3.8 percent rise from the previous month. But soon afterwards, the JGBs set off on an almost uninterrupted upward swing on the June and July output forecasts.
The Trade Ministry said forecast a fall in output of 2.6 percent month-on-month for June and a rise of just 0.9 percent for July.

JGBs were also buoyed by a remark by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita that if the official discount rate was raised prematurely it would negatively affect the economy, which could in turn push down long-term yields.
His statement was in reference to a general argument that Japan's low interest rates are exposing people dependent on interest rate income to a severe financial situation.

After the output data, the key Septemer rose to a high of 124.27, up from 123.27 at Thursday's finish. It ended at 124.15. The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.365 percent, down sharply from 2.470 percent on Thursday.

"The weak output forecasts for June and July suggested that the Bank of Japan would remain quite wary of a credit tightening, as implied by BOJ Governor Matsushita today," said Yasunari Ueno, chief economist at Fuji Securities Co Ltd research group.

"It's a two-tiered economy at the moment. The industrial sector is performing extremely well but the BOJ is watching the consumption side of the economy," said Anthony Limbrick, head of fixed income at Credit Lyonnais. "We do believe that there won't be very much good news for the consumption side of the economy, which we believe is the key to a rate hike," he said.
Investors, including public funds, city and regional banks, and local credit cooperatives, were all on the bid side, accentuating the JGBs' climb, traders said.
Some public funds, possibly including the Postal Savings System, appeared to have bought 20-year JGBs in large lots, some said.

By late Friday trading, cash and futures JGBs had mostly recouped steep losses incurred on Wednesday's BOJ "tankan" corporate sentiment survey, results of which were much stronger than the market had expected.
